entries.riskStatement: GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (CVE-2026-118764) affects glob pattern preprocessing with optimizationLevel >= 2. The locked copy is required by Expo fingerprint build tooling; we have not demonstrated a path from user notes or API data to such patterns. Exhaustion from malicious repository-controlled patterns remains a build-runner concern, not proven impossible.
entries.mitigation: Maintain ephemeral restricted CI jobs, reject untrusted build configuration and user-controlled glob patterns, keep the live npm audit visible, and follow the Expo upstream fix rather than forcing minimatch 11 across semver-major APIs. Recheck reachability and all mobile/OIDC/native smoke after any upstream update.

entries.riskStatement: npm reports this meta-vulnerability through the declared minimatch ^10.2.6 dependency; Expo fingerprint is a Node-side native project hash/build tool, not a demonstrated browser or API handler. That assessment relies on the present dependency graph and upstream analysis, not on a complete native device audit.
entries.mitigation: Do not pass user-controlled filesystem glob expressions to fingerprint in server routes, isolate builds with read-only tokens and restricted runner resources, and track upstream Expo fingerprint migration. Avoid untested direct minimatch overrides; maintain CI/OIDC/Pages/native compatibility gates.

entries.riskStatement: The expo umbrella package is flagged indirectly because its Node build tool depends on @expo/fingerprint and thus minimatch. The npm production scope is an install classification and does not prove bundling into web or native runtime. No untrusted capture-to-glob route was verified.
entries.mitigation: Keep Expo SDK 58/RN 0.88 peer and npm lock verification, prevent automatic dependency overrides, retain native Metro exports and browser OIDC integration tests, and reassess official Expo patch changes before a controlled rebuild; track this meta-finding until the upstream chain is resolved.
